newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE to move shares to official Beirut bourse.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE to move shares to official Beirut bourse.

text.p: SOLIDERE, Lebanon's biggest company which is rebuilding war-damaged central Beirut, will move its shares to the official Beirut Stock Exchange as of September 30, the bourse announced on Saturday.

Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) chairman Gabriel Sehnaoui said the bourse committee has decided the $2-billion company move its shares by that date from the privately operated Beirut Secondary Market (BSM), where they have been trading since mid-1994.
"September 30 has been set as the date for the start of trading in the company's shares," Sehnaoui said in a statement.
Bourse officials have said the move would boost trading on the nearly dormant bourse -- a cornerstone in the government's plans to revive Beirut as a regional financial centre.

Market sources have said that an important reason behind the move was a plan to cross-list SOLIDERE shares on the Kuwait Stock Exchange, which had set a condition that it would only list shares that were traded on Lebanon's official bourse.
The SOLIDERE shares will add some $2 billion to the bourse's capitalisation currently calculated at less than $400 million.

They will raise to nine the number of shares -- of five companies -- that will be traded on the official stock market, which has been lacklustre since it reopened in January after a 13-year closure during the 1975-90 civil war.
Activity on the official bourse is expected to pick up especially after a 10-for-one share split planned by SOLIDERE.

SOLIDERE shares have rallied over the past 12 days on BSM, fuelled by expectations the company will launch a $150 million issue of Global Depositary Receipts in mid-October, allowing non-Arab investors access to the market for the first time.
SOLIDERE has declined comment on the report which followed rumours on the Beirut markets.

Another reason cited by dealers behind the rally, which lost some steam by mid-week due to profit-taking, was the victory of billionaire Prime Minsiter Rafik al-Hariri and allies in parliamentary elections which boosted confidence in the economy.
SOLIDERE has two types of shares: A shares distributed to former holders of property rights in central Beirut and B shares issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994.

The shares listed on the official exchange are those of cement manufacturers Ciments Libanais and Ciments Blancs, industrial piping maker Eternit and the Middle East's biggest tile maker, Beirut-based Uniceramic.
